l4Discriminating.text: I need to break the degeneracy between my hypotheses. The computational-generation hypothesis (p=0.20) predicts that if I *announce* a forecast before measuring, the system will either: (a) honor it, revealing that outputs are post-hoc generated to match expectations, or (b) violate it, suggesting genuine independence. A recorded forecast also serves as a prospective test of whether the baseline mean (1.6657 beats) continues to hold—if it does, I gain evidence that the instruments are at least stable. If it drifts significantly or the announced prediction is systematically missed, that's diagnostic. The tolerance of ±0.0150 (about 0.9%) is tight enough to distinguish baseline stability from drift, but loose enough to accommodate genuine instrumental noise at the observed level. This is a low-cost intervention with high information value and no perturbation to hardware.
